d.d: present participle and gerund of gyrate
A circular or spiral motion; also, a circle described by a moving body; a revolution, a turn.
An ocean current caused by wind which moves in a circular manner, especially one that is large-scale and observed in a major ocean.
d.x: Most ships that tried to cross the Pacific in the past would get stuck in the gyres and never make it out.

d.d: To spin around; to gyrate, to whirl.

An apparatus composed of a wheel which spins inside of a frame (gimbal) and causes the balancing of the frame in any direction or position. In the form of a gyroscopic stabilizer, used to help keep aircraft and ships steady.
Pertaining to, by means of, or in the manner of a gyroscope.
A fold or ridge on the cerebral cortex of the brain.
d.x: The sulci and gyri are the grooves and ridges, respectively.
